chunks: Muthannā ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who performs hajj on behalf of another person, mentioning him in all the stations, he said:
"If he wishes, he may do so, and if he wishes, he may not. Allah knows that he has performed hajj on his behalf; however, he should mention him عند the udhiyah when he slaughters it."

key_terms.اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ: Allah knows the intention and act
key_terms.الْمَوَاطِنِ: the ritual stations or places of the rites

ai.seo_question: When performing hajj on behalf of someone else, must their name be mentioned at every station?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing hajj on behalf of another person. Mentioning the person’s name throughout the rites is optional, because Allah knows the intention and on whose behalf the hajj is being performed. However, the person should mention the one represented at the time of the sacrificial offering.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2970 - It was narrated from Muthanna ibn Abdul-Salam, from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a person performing Hajj on behalf of someone else. Should he mention that person’s name at every station?

"If he wishes, he may do so, and if he wishes, he may not. Allah (swt) knows that he has performed Hajj on their behalf. However, he should mention the person's name when offering the sacrifice (udhiyah) at the time of slaughter."
